title: The Proclamations of Crisis and the Victory of the Son of Mary
english: Sayings concerning the holy Epiphanius, bishop of Cyprus. 1. Saint Epiphanius the bishop recounted that during the time of the blessed Athanasius the Great, maidens surrounding the temple of Serapis were crying out, 'Crisis, Crisis!' The Greeks standing before the blessed Athanasius cried out, 'You ill-born man, tell us what the maidens are crying.' Having replied, he said, 'The maidens cry, Crisis, Crisis; and the Crisis in the Ausonian tongue means tomorrow.' He added, 'Tomorrow you shall see the glory of God.' Subsequently, the death of King Julian was announced. After this happened, they rushed together crying at the temple of Serapis, saying, 'If you did not want him, why did you take his possessions?' 2. The same recounted that there was a driver among the Alexandrians who was the son of Mary the mother. While riding, this man fell; then, having risen, he passed the one who had cast him down and conquered. The crowd shouted, 'The Son of Mary has fallen and has risen and has conquered!' While this voice was still being spoken, the fame concerning the temple of Serapis spread among the people, that the great Theophilus, having ascended, destroyed the idol of Serapis and has become master of the temple. 3. It was made known to the blessed Epiphanius, the bishop of Cyprus, by the abbot of the monastery he held in Palestine, that 'We have not been negligent of your prayers regarding our rule, but with haste we perform even the third and the sixth and the ninth [offices].' title: Prayer, Discipline, and Christ's Blessing
english: Having reproved them, he made it clear to them by saying that they are exposed in their neglect of the other hours of the day, being idle from prayer. For it is necessary for the true monk to hold prayer and psalmody unceasingly within his heart.

The holy Epiphanius once sent word to Abba Hilarion, entreating him and saying, 'Come, let us see ourselves before we depart from the body.' When he arrived, they rejoiced together. While they were eating, a bird was brought. The bishop took it and gave it to Abba Hilarion. The old man said to him, 'Forgive me, for since I received the habit, I have not eaten a sacrificial animal.' The bishop replied to him, 'But I, since I received the habit, have not permitted anyone to sleep holding [resentment] against me, nor did I sleep holding [resentment] against anyone.' The old man said to him, 'Forgive me, for your way of life is greater than mine.'
He the same used to say that the image of Christ, Melchizedek, who blessed Abraham, the root of the Jews; how much more is the truth, Christ, who blesses and sanctifies all those who believe in him.

title: The Discipline of Prayer and Scripture
english: The same said that the prophet David prayed at unseasonable times; he was rising at midnight, calling at dawn, standing at dawn, building at morning, and entreating at evening and noon. For this reason he said: Seven times in the day have you found me.

He said again that the acquisition of books is necessary for those Christians who possess them. For the very sight of books works us to be more sluggish toward sin, and is instead turned toward righteousness.

He said again that the reading of the Scriptures is a great security against sinning. He said again that ignorance of the Scriptures is a great cliff and a deep pit. He said again that not knowing any of the divine laws is a great betrayal of salvation.

The same said that the sins of the righteous are about the lips, but the sins of the impious are from the whole body. Therefore David sings: O Lord, keep watch over my mouth, and a door of restraint about my lips; and: I said, I will guard my ways, so that I may not sin in my tongue.

title: Divine Justice and the Economy of Mercy
english: Beatitudes? And he said: the Decalogue is an equal number to the Egyptian lashes; and the numbering of the beatitudes is an icon of the triple Trinity.

The same man was asked if a single righteous person is enough to slander God, and he said: Yes, for he himself said: Search for one doing judgment and righteousness, and I will be gracious to all the people. 15. The same said that God grants the principal to sinners who repent, just as to the harlot and the tax collector; but to the righteous, he demands both principal and interest. And this is what he was saying to the apostles: If your righteousness does not exceed that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will by no means enter the kingdom of heaven.

He also said this: that God sells righteousness very little to those striving to buy it; a small morsel of bread, a cheap garment, a cold cup, one obol. 16. And he added this: that a man, borrowing from another through poverty or a need for prosperity, confesses grace when he repays, but he repays secretly out of shame. But the Lord God does the opposite: lending secretly before angels and archangels and the righteous, he repays.
